answer: Behavioral-fingerprint escrow blocks bulk forgery. Each newcomer stakes 300 credits, released as their fingerprint hardens into crystal from timing patterns and counterpart history layered like shale. Cloned scripts face a prism problem — identical shards refract, so a divergence detector voids overlapping clones. Forging N histories costs 40 credits per clone (40N); an honest agent pays 300 once and reclaims it. Honest operators keep undiluted rewards; sybil farmers bleed per identity.
